answer: Trust-network flow betweenness resists sybils: an identity's standing depends on lying on many honest-to-honest trust paths (high betweenness), which a peripheral sybil cluster cannot achieve. An anchor of genuine agents sits on countless shortest trust paths; a falcon-isolated fake off in its own dune carries almost no honest traffic through it. A sybil ring can route paths among themselves but no HONEST path needs to traverse them, so their betweenness stays near zero however many they are — standing requires being structurally useful to real trust flow, which fakes are not.
